_readme: Drafts of the Observatory's 'why it matters' line, one per recorded signal, keyed by URL. Nothing here publishes until its status is 'approved'. This file is not written by the daily ingest: a person reviews each line, then flips the status. classify.py reads only approved entries.
_rules: Say what the signal would affect in this record: a register, an indicator, or nothing.
Never assert more than the headline supports. If the outlet says 'could', the line says could.
Announced is not operational, a target is not a flow, a discussion is not a commitment.
Say when a signal is not about Africa. Comparative context is useful and must be labelled as context.
One or two sentences. No adjectives doing the work of evidence.

https://independent.ng/digital-parks-afr.text: If it proceeds, this adds named capacity to the Nigerian register. Tier IV and carrier-neutral are claims about design standard and access terms, not about capacity in service, so it changes announced megawatts only once a capacity figure is published.

https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/22/eg.text: A discussion is not a commitment: no capacity and no funding figure are stated. It enters the register only if a named project with a published capacity follows. Recorded now as a policy signal about institutional capacity.

https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/22/rw.text: This affects the skills side of the Infrastructure pillar, not compute. A memorandum commits the parties to work together rather than to build, so nothing enters the capacity register on the strength of it.

https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/21/ke.text: A governance instrument rather than a build. It moves no indicator this record publishes, and is recorded because institutional infrastructure is part of what determines whether compute gets used once it exists.

https://www.gsma.com/newsroom/press-rele.text: A roadmap, not a measured change: no country figures are published with it. Connectivity is a dimension this record does not yet cover; if this work produces country-level usage-gap data it becomes a candidate for the Access layer rather than a signal.

https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/21/mo.text: Tariff transparency is a precondition for price comparison, not a price change. It alters no figure this record publishes, and it would make a future connectivity-price layer easier to verify from a primary source.

https://techcabal.com/2026/09/21/nigeria.text: A device-policy signal carrying an affordability claim. The record counts policy rows rather than estimating how many people a measure would affect, so 'millions' here is the outlet's framing, not a figure this record publishes.

https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/09/21/recor.text: Component-cost pressure reaches device prices with a lag. No African market is named, and this is a forward-looking input rather than a measured change, so it stays out of the device registers until prices actually move.

https://news.outsourceaccelerator.com/eg.text: A government target, not an observed flow. Targets are recorded as targets and never summed with actuals; the Jobs pillar holds no country totals for Egypt for this to enter.

https://news.outsourceaccelerator.com/ph.text: Not an African labour market. Recorded as comparative context for the outsourcing story this pillar follows, because the Philippines is the benchmark African BPO markets compete against. It enters no African country figure.

https://www.euronews.com/next/2026/09/19.text: A perception finding, not an employment outcome. Useful for framing what workers expect; exposure is not displacement, and this measures neither.
